title: Billing Convention for Licenses Added Near the Order Date or Near the End of a Microsoft 365 Cycle
content:
**Convention.** On a Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) subscription, the days charged on a seat addition's partial-cycle charge follow when the addition is submitted:

- **Billed with the order.** The subscription has never renewed, and the seat addition is submitted no more than six calendar days after the date the cancellation window opened. The partial-cycle charge covers all the days of the cycle.
- **Billed from the next cycle.** The seat addition is not part of the order, and seven or fewer days run from its submission date through the last day of the cycle inclusive. No days are charged, and the licenses are billed from the next cycle.
- **Any other seat addition.** The days charged are not changed by this convention.

The renewal count, the window's opening moment and the seat addition's submission moment are read from the subscription's records.

## Day-count table (hypothetical subscription, never renewed, window opened on 1 January, cycle ending 31 December)

| Seat addition submitted on | Days after the window opened | Days through 31 December inclusive | Days charged |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 January | 6 | 359 | all 365 days of the cycle |
| 8 January | 7 | 358 | not changed by this convention |
| 24 December | — | 8 | not changed by this convention |
| 25 December | — | 7 | none; billed from the next cycle |

**After a renewal.** Once the subscription has renewed, no seat addition is billed with the order, however soon after the new window opens. The seven-day rule at the end of the cycle still applies.

## Hypothetical illustration

On a cycle amount per license of 120.00 USD, a never-renewed subscription adds 4 licenses on 5 January. All 365 days are charged, so the prorated amount is 120.00 times 4, which is 480.00. An addition of 4 licenses on 26 December has no days charged, so its prorated amount is nothing.
